To design a FastAPI endpoint that handles adding items to a shopping cart, we will first create a new text file to store the FastAPI route handler. We will then implement the endpoint using the provided tools.

1. Create a new text file using the `create_text_file` tool to store the FastAPI route handler. The file path must be absolute, and we will name it `app/items.py`.

```
{"name": "create_text_file", "parameters": {"file_path": "E:\\Hackathon\\buddy-agent\\app\\items.py", "encoding": "utf-8", "contents": ""}}
```

2. Implement the FastAPI route handler in the `app/items.py` file. We will define a POST endpoint to handle item addition to the shopping cart.

```
{"name": "create_text_file", "parameters": {"file_path": "E:\\Hackathon\\buddy-agent\\app\\items.py", "encoding": "utf-8", "contents": "from fastapi import FastAPI, Request, Response\r\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel\r\nfrom typing import Dict, List\r\n\r\napp = FastAPI()\r\n\r\nclass Item(BaseModel):\r\n    id: int\r\n    name: str\r\n    price: float\r\n\r\n@app.post(\"/items\")\r\nasync def add_item(item: Item):\r\n    # Forward the request to the cart management microservice\r\n    # Simulate a call to the microservice\r\n    print(f\"Adding item {item.name} to cart...\")\r\n    return Response(\"Item added to cart successfully\", media_type=\"text/plain\")"}}
```

3. The `add_item` function in the `app/items.py` file will forward the request to the cart management microservice. For demonstration purposes, we will simulate a call to the microservice by printing a message to the console.

4. To ensure the endpoint does not perform direct database queries, we will not include any database connection or ORM persistence code in the `app/items.py` file.

5. The `skills` tool can be used to load the complete instructions for the `rest-agent` skill, which includes information on how to implement business logic and forward requests to microservices.

The final FastAPI endpoint design will be stored in the `E:\Hackathon\buddy-agent\app\items.py` file.
